Print and summarize the bootstraps of a grouped network

Source: R/bootstrap_htna.R
print.htna_bootstrap_group.Rd

print() and summary() read the bootstraps of a grouped network: print() shows each cohort's report in turn under its name, and summary() stacks the cohorts' edge tables into one data frame, so the edges of the cohorts can be read and compared together. A grouped network bootstrapped with bootstrap_htna() gives one bootstrap per cohort.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'htna_bootstrap_group'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'htna_bootstrap_group'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

x, object

An htna_bootstrap_group from bootstrap_htna().

...

Passed to the method of each cohort.

Value

print() returns x invisibly. summary() returns a data frame with one row per cohort and edge: a first column group, then the columns of the per-cohort summary (from, to, weight, mean, sd, p_value, sig, ci_lower, ci_upper, cr_lower, cr_upper).

See also

bootstrap_htna(), plot_htna_bootstrap().

Examples

data(human_ai)
grp <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type", group = "phase")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'cluster' (24 sessions), 'actor_type' (9 sessions)
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (18 sessions), 'actor_type' (15 sessions)
boots <- bootstrap_htna(grp, iter = 20, seed = 1)
boots
#> HTNA bootstrap, 2 cohorts
#>

#>   Edge                   Mean     95% CI          p
